column1: What is the fundamental neurological/cognitive event that produces laughter, according to the foundational theory of humor?
column2: A collision between what the mind anticipated and what actually occurred, followed by a rapid reconciliation of that incongruity into a coherent, non-threatening frame.

column1: What are the three essential sequential components present in every joke or comedic structure?
column2: 1) Establishment of a cognitive pathway (predictive trajectory), 2) A violation/swerve away from that pathway, 3) Retroactive recontextualization where setup and punchline cohere into a new logical frame.

column1: Why are incongruity theory, superiority theory, and relief theory best understood as complementary rather than competing?
column2: Because master comedians layer these mechanisms together within a single joke, creating reinforcing structures that produce more powerful and durable laughter than any single mechanism alone.

column1: What mechanism explains how a comedian engineers surprise without it feeling random or confusing?
column2: Information asymmetry and rhythmic release: the comic knows more than the audience, withholds key information, misdirects attention, establishes false patterns, then executes a reversal that recontextualizes everything.

column1: What is the 'narrow band' a comic violation must land within to be perceived as funny rather than threatening or boring?
column2: Between surprise and safety—calibrated magnitude, timing, and moral tenor so the violation feels neither genuinely threatening/painful (causing recoil) nor too obvious/telegraphed (causing boredom).

column1: What happens if a comedic violation feels genuinely threatening, morally abhorrent, or physically painful?
column2: The audience will not laugh; they will recoil instead, because the violation fails the safety condition required for laughter.

column1: What role do structural frameworks play in comedy, per the architectural view of comic construction?
column2: They are tested architectural patterns (not rigid formulas) that reliably generate conditions for laughter, used with conscious intention and strategically broken when appropriate—analogous to chord progressions for a songwriter.

column1: What invariant underlies comedy's fundamental difference from tragedy in temporal/structural terms?
column2: Comedy operates through discontinuity (audience anticipates one trajectory, encounters another), while tragedy derives power from inevitability and accumulation.

column1: Why did specific historical comedic forms (e.g., Commedia dell'arte, Restoration drawing-room comedy, standup) emerge as they did?
column2: They arose from material conditions of performance—economic pressures, available technology, stage architecture, and audience composition—not from aesthetic innovation alone.

column1: What is the timing invariant common to all comedic forms (pratfalls, punchlines, sketch reveals, farce escalation)?
column2: Absolute precision in the rhythm of revelation and reaction—the comedic impulse lives in the milliseconds between setup and payoff, between expectation and subversion.

column1: What happens if a punchline is delivered one beat too early vs. one beat too late?
column2: Too early: it lands flat because the audience hasn't fully locked into the anticipated direction. Too late: the audience preemptively generates the punchline themselves, collapsing the surprise.

column1: What is a 'performance persona' in comedic delivery, and why does it matter?
column2: A theatrical entity distinct from the performer's private self that filters all material, providing consistent logic for tone and perspective; it answers unconscious audience questions (who is speaking, what do they want) and determines audience willingness to follow into uncomfortable or absurdist territory.
